worker: optional absolute deadline (PHYSICAL_SINGLE_CARTON scope only, never init) caps the request NativeDeadline; a reference after receipt or a deadline more than 60 s past refuses with DEADLINE_CLOCK_DOMAIN_MISMATCH (both clocks are Linux CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
each request waits on a per-worker IPC thread; at the deadline the caller is released, that worker is never reused and its late reply is collected in the background

workers are closed in the background under a deadline (a worker ignores SIGTERM; each close takes 5 s)
a pool worker whose plan ended or whose generation is old never joins a pool; it is closed outside the lock

findings: Worker close: SIGTERM is ignored and ResidentMoveItClient.close waits 5 s before SIGKILL. Without a deadline, plan_cycle closes the main worker and every pool worker sequentially before PLAN_READY: about 5 s x (1 + native_check_workers) = 35 s with the example configuration. Unchanged without a deadline (step 4).
Worker cold start (init) measured 3.8 s; a first planner build 9.2 s (cached after observe in the workbench).
contact_candidates takes ~0.6 s of pure Python for a 150x100x100 mm top face (not preemptible).

Pre-existing race without a deadline: a pool worker still initialising when its plan ends can join the next plan's pool (pool_closed is reset by the next start_check_pool), and closes while holding the pool lock. Fixed only on the deadline path here; to be fixed for both with resident workers (step 4).
Finalisation after a complete plan (binding rehash ~1.86 s, register, records) is not aborted by the deadline; its duration is reported (finalize stage of the budget table).
